name: Ibibio
notes: Standard Ibibio Latin orthography as codified by the Ibibio Language Panel and described in Essien (1990), A Grammar of the Ibibio Language, and Essien's The Orthography of the Ibibio Language (Ibibio Language Panel, Calabar). Seven-vowel system /i e a o ɔ u ʌ/ matching the cited PHOIBLE inventory; ⟨ọ⟩ marks the open-mid back vowel /ɔ/ distinct from ⟨o⟩ /o/ (underdotted-vowel convention shared with the closely related Efik orthography, cf. efi.json), and the vowel letter ⟨ʌ⟩ is a direct IPA-symbol borrowing rather than a diacritic variant. ⟨gh⟩ is the single velar fricative /ɣ/ (test 1: g+h would give a stop-plus-glottal-fricative sequence Ibibio does not have) and ⟨kp⟩ the single labial-velar stop /kp/. ⟨n̄⟩ (macron n) is the velar nasal /ŋ/, distinguished from plain ⟨n⟩ /n/; ⟨n̄w⟩ is its labialized allophone-bearing counterpart /ŋʷ/-context digraph, and ⟨ny⟩ the palatal nasal /ɲ/. /h/ and /p/ are marginal (largely loanword) phonemes in Ibibio and are not part of the cited PHOIBLE non-marginal 30-segment count, but are attested letters of the standard alphabet and are mapped here for orthographic completeness. Smoke-tested against the cited Ibibio numerals: ⟨Kèèd⟩ [kèèd] 'one', ⟨Íbà⟩ [íbà] 'two', ⟨Ítá⟩ [ítá] 'three' — each resolves through the mapped consonant/vowel graphemes above (long vowels spelled by doubling the vowel letter, e.g. ⟨èè⟩ = /eː/, matching the cited PHOIBLE length contrast). The underdotted front-vowel letter ⟨ị⟩ and back-vowel letter ⟨ụ⟩ reported in some dialect descriptions (e.g. Ibiono) are left unmapped: the cited 30-segment PHOIBLE inventory for standard Ibibio recognizes no additional vowel qualities beyond the seven above, so encoding them here would assert an uncited contrast. Ibibio is a five-tone (high, mid, rising, falling, low) language with no lexical word stress; tone is not consistently marked in ordinary orthography and is left unencoded here, a documented exemption distinct from stress (docs/quality_tiers.md).
